title.en: Biographies of Fan Sui and Cai Ze
title.raw: 《范睢蔡澤列傳》 Biographies of Fan Sui and Cai Ze

sentences.zh: 范睢者，魏人也，字叔。

translations.literal: Fan Sui was a native of Wei, courtesy name Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui was a man of Wei, courtesy name Shu.

sentences.zh: 游說諸侯，欲事魏王，家貧無以自資，乃先事魏中大夫須賈。

translations.literal: He traveled among the feudal lords as a persuader, wishing to serve the King of Wei, but being poor with no means to support himself, he first served Xu Jia, the central grand master of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled among the feudal lords as a persuader, hoping to serve the King of Wei. But being poor and unable to support himself, he first served Xu Jia, a Grandee of Wei.

sentences.zh: 須賈為魏昭王使於齊，范睢從。

translations.literal: When Xu Jia served as envoy for King Zhao of Wei to Qi, Fan Sui accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jia served as envoy from King Zhao of Wei to Qi, Fan Sui accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 留數月，未得報。

translations.literal: They stayed for several months without receiving a reply.
translations.idiomatic: They remained for several months without receiving any response.

sentences.zh: 齊襄王聞睢辯口，乃使人賜睢金十斤及牛酒，睢辭謝不敢受。

translations.literal: King Xiang of Qi heard of Sui's eloquent speech and sent people to grant Sui ten jin of gold and beef and wine. Sui declined with thanks, not daring to accept.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiang of Qi heard of Sui's eloquent speech and sent emissaries to present him with ten jin of gold along with beef and wine. Sui declined with thanks, not daring to accept.

sentences.zh: 須賈知之，大怒，以為睢持魏國陰事告齊，故得此饋，令睢受其牛酒，還其金。

translations.literal: Xu Jia learned of this and flew into a rage, believing that Sui had revealed Wei's secret affairs to Qi and thus received these gifts. He commanded Sui to accept the beef and wine but return the gold.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia learned of this and flew into a rage, believing that Sui had betrayed Wei's secrets to Qi and thus received these gifts. He ordered Sui to accept the beef and wine but return the gold.

sentences.zh: 既歸，心怒睢，以告魏相。

translations.literal: After returning, he was angry with Sui and reported the matter to the Wei chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, his anger at Sui only deepened, and he reported the affair to the Wei chancellor.

sentences.zh: 魏相，魏之諸公子，曰魏齊。

translations.literal: The Wei chancellor was one of Wei's princes, named Wei Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of Wei was a member of the Wei princely house named Wei Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏齊大怒，使舍人笞擊睢，折脅摺齒。

translations.literal: Wei Qi was furious and had his retainers flog Sui, breaking his ribs and knocking out his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qi flew into a rage and ordered his retainers to beat Sui, breaking his ribs and knocking out his teeth.

sentences.zh: 睢詳死，即卷以簀，置廁中。

translations.literal: Sui feigned death, was rolled up in a mat, and placed in the latrine.
translations.idiomatic: Sui feigned death, so they rolled him in a mat and placed him in the latrine.

sentences.zh: 賓客飲者醉，更溺睢，故僇辱以懲後，令無妄言者。

translations.literal: The drinking guests got drunk and further urinated on Sui, thus humiliating him to punish others later and ensure no one dared speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: The drinking guests got drunk and further urinated on Sui, deliberately humiliating him to deter others and ensure no one dared speak rashly again.

sentences.zh: 睢從簀中謂守者曰：「公能出我，我必厚謝公。」

translations.literal: From within the mat Sui said to the guard: 'If you can release me, I will certainly reward you generously.'
translations.idiomatic: From within the mat Sui told the guard: 'If you can release me, I will certainly reward you generously.'

sentences.zh: 守者乃請出棄簀中死人。

translations.literal: The guard then requested permission to throw out the dead man in the mat.
translations.idiomatic: The guard then requested permission to dispose of the dead man wrapped in the mat.

sentences.zh: 魏齊醉，曰：「可矣。」

translations.literal: Wei Qi, being drunk, said: 'Very well.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qi, being drunk, said: 'Very well.'

sentences.zh: 范睢得出。

translations.literal: Fan Sui escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui escaped.

sentences.zh: 後魏齊悔，復召求之。

translations.literal: Later Wei Qi regretted this and again sent people to seek him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Qi regretted his actions and sent people to summon him again.

sentences.zh: 魏人鄭安平聞之，乃遂操范睢亡，伏匿，更名姓曰張祿。

translations.literal: A man of Wei named Zheng Anping heard of this, then took Fan Sui and fled; they hid themselves and changed his surname and given name to Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: A Wei native named Zheng Anping heard of this and led Fan Sui in flight. They hid themselves and changed his name to Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 當此時，秦昭王使謁者王稽於魏。

translations.literal: At this time, King Zhao of Qin sent the usher Wang Ji to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Around this time, King Zhao of Qin dispatched the usher Wang Ji to Wei.

sentences.zh: 鄭安平詐為卒，侍王稽。

translations.literal: Zheng Anping disguised himself as a soldier and served Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Anping disguised himself as a common soldier to serve Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 王稽問：「魏有賢人可與俱西游者乎？」

translations.literal: Wang Ji asked: 'Does Wei have any worthy men who could travel west with me?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji inquired: 'Are there any worthy men in Wei who might journey west with me?'

sentences.zh: 鄭安平曰：「臣里中有張祿先生，欲見君，言天下事。

translations.literal: Zheng Anping said: 'In my village there is Master Zhang Lu who wishes to see you and discuss affairs of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Anping replied: 'There lives a Master Zhang Lu in my village who wishes to meet you and speak of matters under heaven.

sentences.zh: 其人有仇，不敢晝見。」

translations.literal: That man has enemies and dares not meet in daylight.'
translations.idiomatic: This man has enemies and cannot risk meeting in broad daylight.'

sentences.zh: 王稽曰：「夜與俱來。」

translations.literal: Wang Ji said: 'Bring him at night.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said: 'Bring him under cover of night.'

sentences.zh: 鄭安平夜與張祿見王稽。

translations.literal: Zheng Anping brought Zhang Lu to see Wang Ji at night.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Zheng Anping brought Zhang Lu to meet Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 語未究，王稽知范睢賢，謂曰：「先生待我於三亭之南。」

translations.literal: Their conversation was not yet finished when Wang Ji recognized Fan Sui's worth and said: 'Master, wait for me south of the three pavilions.'
translations.idiomatic: Before their conversation had concluded, Wang Ji recognized Fan Sui's talents and said: 'Master, await me south of the three pavilions.'

sentences.zh: 與私約而去。

translations.literal: They made a private agreement and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They reached a secret understanding and left.

sentences.zh: 王稽辭魏去，過載范睢入秦。

translations.literal: Wang Ji bid farewell to Wei and departed, taking Fan Sui with him to enter Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji took his leave of Wei and set out, bringing Fan Sui along into Qin territory.

sentences.zh: 至湖，望見車騎從西來。

translations.literal: When they reached Hu, they saw carriages and riders approaching from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Hu, they spotted a procession of carriages and horsemen approaching from the west.

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「彼來者為誰？」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Who are those approaching?'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui asked: 'Who comes there?'

sentences.zh: 王稽曰：「秦相穰侯東行縣邑。」

translations.literal: Wang Ji said: 'The Qin chancellor Lord Rang is touring the eastern counties.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji explained: 'It is Lord Rang, Qin's chancellor, making his rounds through the eastern counties.'

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「吾聞穰侯專秦權，惡內諸侯客，此恐辱我，我寧且匿車中。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'I have heard that Lord Rang monopolizes Qin's power and hates receiving guests from the various lords. This might bring humiliation to me. I would rather hide in the carriage for now.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'I understand Lord Rang holds Qin's power in his grip and detests hosting visitors from other states. This could bring me humiliation. I'd best conceal myself in the carriage for the moment.'

sentences.zh: 有頃，穰侯果至，勞王稽，因立車而語曰：「關東有何變？」

translations.literal: After a while, Lord Rang indeed arrived. He greeted Wang Ji, then stood by the carriage and asked: 'What changes have there been east of the pass?'
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Lord Rang arrived as expected. He exchanged greetings with Wang Ji, then stood beside the carriage and inquired: 'What news from east of the pass?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: He said: 'None.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'None at all.'

sentences.zh: 又謂王稽曰：「謁君得無與諸侯客子俱來乎？

translations.literal: He again asked Wang Ji: 'Usher, you didn't happen to bring any guests from the various lords with you, did you?
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Wang Ji: 'Usher, did you by chance bring any visitors from other states along with you?

sentences.zh: 無益，徒亂人國耳。」

translations.literal: They are of no benefit; they only disrupt people's states.'
translations.idiomatic: They serve no useful purpose; they merely sow chaos in people's kingdoms.'

sentences.zh: 王稽曰：「不敢。」

translations.literal: Wang Ji said: 'I would not dare.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji said: 'I would never dare.'

sentences.zh: 即別去。

translations.literal: Then he took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he departed.

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「吾聞穰侯智士也，其見事遲，鄉者疑車中有人，忘索之。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'I have heard that Lord Rang is a wise man, but he is slow to perceive matters. Just now he suspected there was someone in the carriage but forgot to search it.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'I understand Lord Rang to be a man of wisdom, but his perceptions are slow. Just now he suspected someone was hiding in the carriage yet forgot to have it searched.'

sentences.zh: 於是范睢下車走，曰：「此必悔之。」

translations.literal: Thus, Fan Sui got out of the carriage and ran, saying: 'He will certainly regret this.'
translations.idiomatic: At this, Fan Sui leaped from the carriage and ran, exclaiming: 'He will surely come to regret this.'

sentences.zh: 行十餘里，果使騎還索車中，無客，乃已。

translations.literal: After walking more than ten li, sure enough he sent riders back to search the carriage. Finding no guest, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After traveling more than ten li, sure enough Lord Rang sent horsemen back to search the carriage. Finding no one inside, they gave up the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 王稽遂與范睢入咸陽。

translations.literal: Wang Ji then entered Xianyang with Fan Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji then proceeded to Xianyang with Fan Sui.

sentences.zh: 已報使，因言曰：「魏有張祿先生，天下辯士也。

translations.literal: Having already reported to the envoy, he then said: 'Wei has Master Zhang Lu, an eloquent scholar of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Having already made his report to the king, Wang Ji then said: 'Wei has a Master Zhang Lu, one of the world's most eloquent scholars.

sentences.zh: 曰『秦王之國危於累卵，得臣則安。

translations.literal: He said: 'The King's state is endangered like piled eggs; with me it will be safe.
translations.idiomatic: He declares: 'Your Majesty's kingdom is in peril like a stack of eggs; with me as minister, it will be secure.

sentences.zh: 然不可以書傳也』。

translations.literal: However, this cannot be transmitted in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this counsel cannot be committed to writing.

sentences.zh: 臣故載來。」

translations.literal: I have therefore brought him.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have brought him here.'

sentences.zh: 秦王弗信，使舍食草具。

translations.literal: The King of Qin did not believe him and had him lodged where he ate fodder and straw.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin remained skeptical and had Fan Sui housed in humble quarters where he ate fodder mixed with straw.

sentences.zh: 待命歲餘。

translations.literal: He waited for orders for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He awaited his summons for over a year.

sentences.zh: 當是時，昭王已立三十六年。

translations.literal: At this time, King Zhao had already been established for thirty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, King Zhao had reigned for thirty-six years.

sentences.zh: 南拔楚之鄢郢，楚懷王幽死於秦。

translations.literal: To the south he captured Ying and Yiling of Chu, King Huai of Chu was imprisoned and died in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, Qin captured Ying and Yiling from Chu. King Huai of Chu was imprisoned and died in Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦東破齊。

translations.literal: Qin broke Qi in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Qin smashed Qi in the east.

sentences.zh: 湣王嘗稱帝，後去之。

translations.literal: King Min once claimed the imperial title, later abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: King Min once proclaimed himself emperor, but later renounced the title.

sentences.zh: 數困三晉。

translations.literal: Several times he trapped the three Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly placed the three Jin states in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 厭天下辯士，無所信。

translations.literal: He disliked the world's eloquent scholars, trusted none.
translations.idiomatic: He grew weary of the world's eloquent persuaders and trusted none of them.

sentences.zh: 穰侯，華陽君，昭王母宣太后之弟也；

translations.literal: Lord Rang, Lord Huayang—these were younger brothers of King Zhao's mother, Queen Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Rang and Lord Huayang were younger brothers of King Zhao's mother, Queen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 而涇陽君、高陵君皆昭王同母弟也。

translations.literal: Lord Jingyang and Lord Gaoling were all full brothers of King Zhao by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Jingyang and Lord Gaoling were King Zhao's full brothers by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 穰侯相，三人者更將，有封邑，以太后故，私家富重於王室。

translations.literal: Lord Rang was chancellor, these three alternated as generals, had fief cities, because of the Queen Mother's influence, their private families were richer and more powerful than the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Rang served as chancellor while these three took turns as generals and held fief cities. Thanks to the Queen Mother's influence, their private fortunes outweighed the royal treasury.

sentences.zh: 及穰侯為秦將，且欲越韓、魏而伐齊綱壽，欲以廣其陶封。

translations.literal: When Lord Rang became Qin general, he also wished to cross Han and Wei to attack Qi's Gangshou, wishing to expand his fief of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Rang became Qin's general, he also sought to bypass Han and Wei to attack Qi's Gangshou, hoping to enlarge his fief of Tao.

sentences.zh: 范睢乃上書曰：

translations.literal: Fan Sui then submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui then presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞明主立政，有功者不得不賞，有能者不得不官，勞大者其祿厚，功多者其爵尊，能治眾者其官大。

translations.literal: I have heard that enlightened rulers establish governance where those with merit must be rewarded, those with ability must be appointed, those with great labor receive thick salaries, those with much merit receive noble ranks, those able to govern the masses receive great offices.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that enlightened rulers establish governance where merit demands reward, ability demands appointment, great labor brings generous salaries, abundant merit brings exalted rank, and skill in governing multitudes brings high office.

sentences.zh: 故無能者不敢當職焉，有能者亦不得蔽隱。

translations.literal: Thus, those without ability dare not undertake positions, those with ability also must not be concealed and hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, the incompetent dare not assume positions, while the capable must not be concealed or hidden away.

sentences.zh: 使以臣之言為可，願行而益利其道；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds my words acceptable, I wish to implement them and further benefit the way;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty deems my words acceptable, I wish to put them into practice and further the beneficial way.

sentences.zh: 以臣之言為不可，久留臣無為也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds my words unacceptable, keeping me long serves no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty finds my words unacceptable, detaining me longer serves no purpose.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「庸主賞所愛而罰所惡；

translations.literal: The saying goes: 'Common lords reward those they love and punish those they hate;
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb states: 'Common rulers reward their favorites and punish their enemies;

sentences.zh: 明主則不然，賞必加於有功，而刑必斷於有罪。」

translations.literal: Enlightened rulers are not like this—rewards must go to those with merit, punishments must be meted out to those with crime.'
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened rulers do not act this way—rewards must be given to those with merit, punishments must be applied to those with crimes.'

sentences.zh: 今臣之胸不足以當椹質，而要不足以待斧鉞，豈敢以疑事嘗試於王哉！

translations.literal: Now my chest is not sufficient to match the executioner's block, my waist not sufficient to await the axe. How dare I test doubtful matters on Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Now my chest is not broad enough for the executioner's block, my waist not sturdy enough to await the axe. How would I dare test doubtful matters on Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 雖以臣為賤人而輕辱，獨不重任臣者之無反復於王邪？

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty considers me a base person and lightly humiliates me, do you not value that those who entrust ministers to you show no duplicity toward Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty regards me as a lowly person and casually humiliates me, do you not value that those who recommend ministers to you show unwavering loyalty to Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 且臣聞周有砥砨，宋有結綠，梁有縣藜，楚有和樸，此四寶者，土之所生，良工之所失也，而為天下名器。

translations.literal: Moreover, I have heard that Zhou has whetstones, Song has knotted jade, Liang has hanging smartweed, Chu has harmonious catalpa—these four treasures are born of the soil, lost by skilled artisans, yet become famous vessels of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, I have heard that Zhou possesses whetstones, Song has knotted jade, Liang has hanging smartweed, Chu has harmonious catalpa—these four treasures are born from the earth, lost by master craftsmen, yet become renowned vessels throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 然則聖王之所棄者，獨不足以厚國家乎？

translations.literal: Then are the things that sage kings have discarded alone insufficient to enrich the state?
translations.idiomatic: Then are the things that sage kings have cast aside alone insufficient to strengthen the state?

sentences.zh: 臣聞善厚家者取之於國，善厚國者取之於諸侯。

translations.literal: I have heard that those who are good at enriching their families take from the state, those who are good at enriching the state take from the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those skilled at enriching their families take from the state, those skilled at enriching the state take from the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 天下有明主則諸侯不得擅厚者，何也？

translations.literal: When the world has an enlightened ruler, why do the feudal lords not dare to monopolize enrichment?
translations.idiomatic: When the world has an enlightened ruler, why do the feudal lords not dare monopolize wealth?

sentences.zh: 為其割榮也。

translations.literal: Because they would divide their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Because they would divide up their glory.

sentences.zh: 良醫知病人之死生，而聖主明於成敗之事，利則行之，害則捨之，疑則少嘗之，雖舜禹復生，弗能改已。

translations.literal: A good physician knows a sick person's life or death, a sage ruler is enlightened about matters of success and failure—benefit then implement, harm then abandon, doubt then test a little, though Shun and Yu were reborn, they could not change what is already done.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled physician knows whether a patient will live or die, a sage ruler is clear about matters of success and failure—benefit then act, harm then abandon, doubt then test cautiously, even if Shun and Yu were reborn, they could not change what has already been done.

sentences.zh: 語之至者，臣不敢載之於書，其淺者又不足聽也。

translations.literal: Words that go to extremes, I dare not load onto the book; those that are shallow are again insufficient to listen to.
translations.idiomatic: Words that are too extreme I dare not commit to writing; those that are too shallow are again unworthy of attention.

sentences.zh: 意者臣愚而不概於王心邪？

translations.literal: Perhaps I am foolish and do not match Your Majesty's heart?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps I am foolish and do not align with Your Majesty's intentions?

sentences.zh: 亡其言臣者賤而不可用乎？

translations.literal: Or is there no one who speaks of ministers who is base and cannot be used?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it that the person who speaks on my behalf is lowly and cannot be employed?

sentences.zh: 自非然者，臣願得少賜游觀之閒，望見顏色。

translations.literal: If it is not so, I wish to obtain a little granted leisure for wandering and viewing, to gaze upon Your Majesty's countenance.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not the case, I wish to receive a small grant of leisure for strolling and viewing, to behold Your Majesty's countenance.

sentences.zh: 一語無效，請伏斧質。

translations.literal: If one word is ineffective, I beg to prostrate myself upon the axe and block.
translations.idiomatic: If a single word proves ineffective, I beg to submit myself to the axe and executioner's block.

sentences.zh: 於是秦昭王大說，乃謝王稽，使以傳車召范睢。

translations.literal: Thus, King Zhao of Qin was greatly delighted, apologized to Wang Ji, and sent a relay carriage to summon Fan Sui.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin was greatly pleased and apologized to Wang Ji, then sent a relay carriage to summon Fan Sui.

sentences.zh: 於是范睢乃得見於離宮，詳為不知永巷而入其中。

translations.literal: Thus, Fan Sui was able to be seen at the detached palace, feigning ignorance of the Yong Alley and entering it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui was thus granted an audience in the detached palace, feigning ignorance of the Yong Alley and entering it.

sentences.zh: 王來而宦者怒，逐之，曰：「王至！」

translations.literal: The king came, but the eunuch was angry and drove Fan Sui away, saying: 'The king arrives!'
translations.idiomatic: The king arrived, but the eunuch was angry and drove Fan Sui away, saying: 'The king arrives!'

sentences.zh: 范睢繆為曰：「秦安得王？

translations.literal: Fan Sui falsely said, "How could Qin have a king?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui deliberately provoked them: "How can Qin be said to have a king?

sentences.zh: 秦獨有太后、穰侯耳。」

translations.literal: Qin has only the Queen Mother and Lord Rang."
translations.idiomatic: It has only the Queen Mother and Lord Rang."

sentences.zh: 欲以感怒昭王。

translations.literal: He wished to provoke King Zhao's anger.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to provoke King Zhao to anger.

sentences.zh: 昭王至，聞其與宦者爭言，遂延迎，謝曰：「寡人宜以身受命久矣，會義渠之事急，寡人旦暮自請太后；

translations.literal: King Zhao arrived, heard him disputing with the eunuch, then prolonged the welcome, apologized: 'I should have received your command in person long ago, but meeting with urgent matters of Yiqu, I morning and evening begged the Queen Mother;
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao arrived and heard Fan Sui disputing with the eunuch. He prolonged the welcome and apologized: 'I should have received your command in person long ago, but urgent matters with Yiqu intervened. I begged the Queen Mother morning and evening;

sentences.zh: 今義渠之事已，寡人乃得受命。

translations.literal: Now the Yiqu matter is finished, I then get to receive your command.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Yiqu matters are resolved, I can finally receive your command.

sentences.zh: 竊閔然不敏，敬執賓主之禮。」

translations.literal: Secretly piteous and insensitive, respectfully hold the rites of host and guest.'
translations.idiomatic: Secretly I pity my insensitivity. I respectfully observe the rites between host and guest.'

sentences.zh: 范睢辭讓。

translations.literal: Fan Sui declined and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui declined with modesty.

sentences.zh: 是日觀范睢之見者，群臣莫不灑然變色易容者。

translations.literal: Those who watched Fan Sui's audience that day, among the ministers, all changed color and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister who witnessed Fan Sui's audience that day blanched and lost composure.

sentences.zh: 秦王屏左右，宮中虛無人。

translations.literal: The King of Qin screened left and right, the palace was empty of people.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin dismissed all attendants; the palace was empty.

sentences.zh: 秦王跽而請曰：「先生何以幸教寡人？」

translations.literal: The King of Qin knelt and requested, "Master, by what favor will you instruct me?"
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin knelt and pleaded, "Master, what good fortune brings me your instruction?"

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「唯唯。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Yes, yes.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'Indeed, indeed.'

sentences.zh: 有閒，秦王復跽而請曰：「先生何以幸教寡人？」

translations.literal: After a pause, the King of Qin again knelt and requested, "Master, by what favor will you instruct me?"
translations.idiomatic: After a while, the King of Qin knelt again and pleaded, "Master, what good fortune brings me your instruction?"

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「唯唯。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Yes, yes.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'Indeed, indeed.'

sentences.zh: 若是者三。

translations.literal: This happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: This happened three times.

sentences.zh: 秦王跽曰：「先生卒不幸教寡人邪？」

translations.literal: The King of Qin knelt and said, "Master, will you finally not instruct me?"
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin knelt and said, "Master, will you truly refuse to instruct me?"

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「非敢然也。

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'I do not dare so.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'I would not dare so.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昔者呂尚之遇文王也，身為漁父而釣於渭濱耳。

translations.literal: I have heard that formerly when Lü Shang encountered King Wen, his body was as a fisherman fishing on the Wei River bank.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Lü Shang encountered King Wen of old, he was but a fisherman casting his line on the banks of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 若是者，交疏也。

translations.literal: Like this, the relationship is distant.
translations.idiomatic: Such encounters create distant relationships.

sentences.zh: 已說而立為太師，載與俱歸者，其言深也。

translations.literal: Already persuaded and established as grand master, loaded and returned together with him—his words were deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once persuaded, he was established as grand master and taken home in a carriage—such were the depths of his counsel.

sentences.zh: 故文王遂收功於呂尚而卒王天下。

translations.literal: Thus, King Wen then received merit from Lü Shang and finally became king of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, King Wen reaped the benefits from Lü Shang and ultimately became ruler of all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄉使文王疏呂尚而不與深言，是周無天子之德，而文武無與成其王業也。

translations.literal: Had King Wen distanced Lü Shang and not spoken deeply with him, Zhou would lack the virtue of a Son of Heaven, and Wen and Wu would have been unable to complete their royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Had King Wen distanced Lü Shang without deep conversation, Zhou would lack the virtue of a true Son of Heaven, and Wen and Wu would never have completed their royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 今臣羈旅之臣也，交疏於王，而所願陳者皆匡君之事，處人骨肉之閒，願效愚忠而未知王之心也。

translations.literal: Now your minister is a fettered wanderer, distantly related to the king, yet desires to correct all the lord's affairs in the state. Though placed between bone and flesh, he wishes to display foolish loyalty but does not know the king's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am but a fettered wanderer, distantly acquainted with Your Majesty, yet I desire to rectify all the affairs of the state. Though situated among the king's closest kin, I wish to offer my foolish loyalty but cannot fathom Your Majesty's heart.

sentences.zh: 此所以王三問而不敢對者也。

translations.literal: This is why Your Majesty has asked three times and I dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Your Majesty has asked three times and I dared not respond.

sentences.zh: 臣非有畏而不敢言也。

translations.literal: Your minister is not afraid—he simply dares not speak.
translations.idiomatic: I am not afraid to speak—I simply dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 臣知今日言之於前而明日伏誅於後，然臣不敢避也。

translations.literal: Your servant knows that to speak today before you and be executed tomorrow—I yet dare not avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: I know that speaking today may bring execution tomorrow, yet I dare not avoid speaking.

sentences.zh: 大王信行臣之言，死不足以為臣患，亡不足以為臣憂，漆身為厲被髪為狂不足以為臣恥。

translations.literal: If the great king trusts and carries out your servant's words, death is insufficient to be your servant's worry, flight insufficient to be your servant's sorrow, painting the body as a leper and letting the hair go wild as a madman insufficient to be your servant's shame.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty trusts and implements my words, death cannot trouble me, exile cannot sadden me, painting my body like a leper or letting my hair go wild like a madman cannot shame me.

sentences.zh: 且以五帝之聖焉而死，三王之仁焉而死，五伯之賢焉而死，烏獲、任鄙之力焉而死，成荊、孟賁、王慶忌、夏育之勇焉而死。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the holiness of the Five Emperors—then death; with the benevolence of the Three Kings—then death; with the worthiness of the Five Hegemons—then death; with the strength of Wu Huo and Ren Bi—then death; with the bravery of Cheng Jing, Meng Ben, Wang Qingji, and Xia Yu—then death.
translations.idiomatic: Even the holiness of the Five Emperors ends in death, the benevolence of the Three Kings ends in death, the worthiness of the Five Hegemons ends in death, the strength of Wu Huo and Ren Bi ends in death, the bravery of Cheng Jing, Meng Ben, Wang Qingji, and Xia Yu ends in death.

sentences.zh: 死者，人之所必不免也。

translations.literal: Death is what no person can certainly avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Death is what no one can avoid.

sentences.zh: 處必然之勢，可以少有補於秦，此臣之所大願也，臣又何患哉！

translations.literal: Placed in an inevitable situation, one can still have a little to supplement Qin—this is your servant's great wish; what worry would your servant have!
translations.idiomatic: Placed in an inevitable position, I can still offer some small benefit to Qin. This is my great wish—what worries do I have!

sentences.zh: 伍子胥橐載而出昭關，夜行晝伏，至於陵水，無以糊其口，厀行蒲伏，稽首肉袒，鼓腹吹篪，乞食於吳市，卒興吳國，闔閭為伯。

translations.literal: Wu Zixu bagged and carried his way out of Zhaoguan, walking by night and hiding by day, reaching Ling Water; with nothing to paste his mouth, he went on his knees crawling prostrate, bowed his head and bared his flesh, drummed his belly and blew the xiao, begged food in Wu's market, and finally raised Wu so that Helü became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu carried his belongings and fled through Zhaoguan, traveling by night and hiding by day until he reached Ling Water. With nothing to fill his mouth, he crawled on his knees, bowed his head and bared his flesh, drummed his belly and played the xiao flute, begging for food in Wu's marketplace. In the end he raised up the state of Wu, making Helü a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 使臣得盡謀如伍子胥，加之以幽囚，終身不復見，是臣之說行也，臣又何憂？

translations.literal: If your servant could exhaust his plans like Wu Zixu, with dark imprisonment added so that he would never again be seen all his life—your servant's persuasion would be carried out; what sorrow would your servant have?
translations.idiomatic: If I could exhaust my plans like Wu Zixu, even if imprisoned in darkness and never seen again for life, my counsel would be implemented—what sorrow would I have?

sentences.zh: 箕子、接輿漆身為厲，被髪為狂，無益於主。

translations.literal: Jizi and Jie Yu painted their bodies as lepers and let their hair go wild as madmen, bringing no benefit to their lord.
translations.idiomatic: jizi and Jie Yu painted their bodies like lepers and let their hair go wild like madmen, but brought no benefit to their lords.

sentences.zh: 假使臣得同行於箕子，可以有補於所賢之主，是臣之大榮也，臣有何恥？

translations.literal: Suppose your servant could walk the same path as Jizi and have something to supplement a worthy lord—that would be your servant's great honor; what shame would your servant have?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I could accompany jizi and bring benefit to a worthy lord—that would be my great honor. What shame would I have?

sentences.zh: 臣之所恐者，獨恐臣死之後，天下見臣之盡忠而身死，因以是杜口裹足，莫肯鄉秦耳。

translations.literal: What your servant fears is only that after your servant dies, the world will see your servant's exhausted loyalty and bodily death, and because of this will stop their mouths and bind their feet, none willing to turn toward Qin.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear is only that after my death, the world will see my utter loyalty and death, and because of this they will shut their mouths and bind their feet, none willing to come to Qin.

sentences.zh: 足下上畏太后之嚴，下惑於姦臣之態，居深宮之中，不離阿保之手，終身迷惑，無與昭姦。

translations.literal: Your Excellency fears the Queen Mother's severity above, and below is confused by treacherous ministers' appearances. Dwelling in the deep palace, never leaving the wet nurses' hands, lifetime confused, none to illuminate the treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency above fears the Queen Mother's severity; below you are confused by treacherous ministers' demeanor. Dwelling in the deep palace, never leaving the wet nurses' hands, you are confused all your life, with no one to illuminate the treachery.

sentences.zh: 大者宗廟滅覆，小者身以孤危，此臣之所恐耳。

translations.literal: In the great case the ancestral temples would be extinguished and overturned; in the small case your person would be isolated and endangered—this is what your servant fears.
translations.idiomatic: At worst the ancestral temples would be extinguished and overturned, at least Your Majesty's person would be isolated and in danger—this is what I fear.

sentences.zh: 若夫窮辱之事，死亡之患，臣不敢畏也。

translations.literal: As for matters of poverty and humiliation, the troubles of death and life—your servant dares not fear them.
translations.idiomatic: As for matters of poverty and humiliation, dangers of death and life, I dare not fear them.

sentences.zh: 臣死而秦治，是臣死賢於生。」

translations.literal: If your servant dies and Qin is orderly, then your servant's death is worthier than life.'
translations.idiomatic: If I die and Qin is orderly, this means my death is better than life.'

sentences.zh: 秦王跽曰：「先生是何言也！

translations.literal: The King of Qin knelt and said, "Master, what words are these!
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin knelt and said, "Master, how can you say such a thing!

sentences.zh: 夫秦國辟遠，寡人愚不肖，先生乃幸辱至於此，是天以寡人慁先生而存先王之宗廟也。

translations.literal: Qin is remote, and I am foolish and unworthy; Master has graciously come here, which is Heaven using me to trouble Master in order to preserve the ancestral temples of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Qin lies far away, and I am foolish and unworthy. Yet Master has graciously come here; this is Heaven sending you to me to preserve the ancestral temples of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 寡人得受命於先生，是天所以幸先王，而不棄其孤也。

translations.literal: That I may receive commands from Master is Heaven favoring the former kings and not abandoning their orphan.
translations.idiomatic: That I may receive your commands is Heaven's favor to the former kings, for it has not abandoned their orphan.

sentences.zh: 先生柰何而言若是！

translations.literal: Master how speak like this!
translations.idiomatic: How can Master speak like this!

sentences.zh: 事無小大，上及太后，下至大臣，願先生悉以教寡人，無疑寡人也。」

translations.literal: In matters great and small, from the Queen Mother above down to the ministers below, I wish Master to teach me fully; do not doubt me."
translations.idiomatic: In matters great or small, from the Queen Mother above to the ministers below, I ask you to teach me everything. Do not hold doubts about me."

sentences.zh: 范睢拜，秦王亦拜。

translations.literal: Fan Sui bowed, and the King of Qin also bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui bowed, the King of Qin also bowed.

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「大王之國，四塞以為固，北有甘泉、谷口，南帶涇、渭，右隴、蜀，左關、阪，奮擊百萬，戰車千乘，利則出攻，不利則入守，此王者之地也。

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'The great king's state is blocked on four sides as solid ground; north it has Ganquan and Gukou, south it girds the Jing and Wei, right Long and Shu, left Guan and Ban—can rouse a million strikers and a thousand war chariots; when favorable it attacks outward, when unfavorable it guards within—this is a king's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'Your Majesty's state is secured by barriers on all four sides. To the north it has Ganquan and Gukou; to the south it is girded by the Jing and Wei rivers; to the west it has Long and Shu; to the east it has the passes and slopes. It can rouse a million fighters and a thousand war chariots. When conditions are favorable, it can attack outward; when they are not, it can withdraw and defend. This is territory fit for a king.

sentences.zh: 民怯於私鬬而勇於公戰，此王者之民也。

translations.literal: The people are cowardly in private fights but brave in public war—this is a king's people.
translations.idiomatic: The people are cowardly in private fights but brave in public wars—this is a king's people.

sentences.zh: 王并此二者而有之。

translations.literal: The king combines both of these.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty combines both of these.

sentences.zh: 夫以秦卒之勇，車騎之眾，以治諸侯，譬若施韓盧而搏蹇兔也，霸王之業可致也，而群臣莫當其位。

translations.literal: With the bravery of Qin's troops and the multitude of chariots and riders, to govern the feudal lords is like setting Han Lu upon a lame rabbit—the hegemon-king's enterprise can be attained, yet the ministers none match their positions.
translations.idiomatic: With Qin's troops' bravery and chariots and riders' multitude, to govern the feudal lords, it is like applying Han Lu to attack a lame rabbit—the hegemon and king's enterprise can be achieved, yet the ministers none match their positions.

sentences.zh: 至今閉關十五年，不敢窺兵於山東者，是穰侯為秦謀不忠，而大王之計有所失也。」

translations.literal: To this day closing the pass for fifteen years, not daring to spy with troops in Shandong—this is Lord Rang planning disloyally for Qin, while the king's plans have some loss.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet to this day Qin has closed its passes for fifteen years and has not dared send troops east of the mountains. This shows that Lord Rang has not planned loyally for Qin, and that Your Majesty's own strategy has suffered some loss.'

sentences.zh: 秦王跽曰：「寡人願聞失計。」

translations.literal: The King of Qin knelt and said, "I wish to hear where the plan is mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin knelt and said, "I wish to hear how the plan fails."

sentences.zh: 然左右多竊聽者，范睢恐，未敢言內，先言外事，以觀秦王之俯仰。

translations.literal: However, on left and right many were secretly listening; Fan Sui feared and did not dare speak of inner matters, and first spoke of outer affairs to observe the King of Qin's inclinations.
translations.idiomatic: However, there were many secretly listening on left and right. Fan Sui feared and did not dare speak of inner matters first, instead spoke of outer affairs to observe the King of Qin's responses.

sentences.zh: 因進曰：「夫穰侯越韓、魏而攻齊綱壽，非計也。

translations.literal: He then advanced and said, "For Lord Rang to cross Han and Wei to attack Qi's Gangshou is not a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui stepped forward and said, "It is no sound strategy for Lord Rang to march through Han and Wei to attack Gangshou in Qi.

sentences.zh: 少出師則不足以傷齊，多出師則害於秦。

translations.literal: If few troops are sent, they will be insufficient to harm Qi; if many are sent, Qin itself will suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: Few troops sent then insufficient to harm Qi, many troops sent then harmful to Qin.

sentences.zh: 臣意王之計，欲少出師而悉韓、魏之兵也，則不義矣。

translations.literal: Your servant supposes the king's plan wishes to send out few troops yet use all of Han and Wei's troops—that would be unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty's plan is to send out few troops of your own while exhausting the armies of Han and Wei. That would be unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 今見與國之不親也，越人之國而攻，可乎？

translations.literal: Now seeing that allied states are not close, to cross others' states and attack—is this permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Now seeing that allied states are not close, crossing others' states to attack—is this acceptable?

sentences.zh: 其於計疏矣。

translations.literal: As to the plan, it is flawed.
translations.idiomatic: This plan is flawed.

sentences.zh: 且昔齊湣王南攻楚，破軍殺將，再辟地千里，而齊尺寸之地無得焉者，豈不欲得地哉，形勢不能有也。

translations.literal: Formerly King Min of Qi attacked Chu in the south, defeated armies and killed generals, and twice opened a thousand li of territory, yet Qi gained not an inch of land. Was it because he did not want land? The situation made it impossible to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Consider King Min of Qi: he attacked Chu to the south, defeated armies, killed generals, and opened up territory by the thousand li, yet Qi gained not an inch. It was not that he did not want the land; the strategic situation made it impossible to keep.

sentences.zh: 諸侯見齊之罷獘，君臣之不和也，興兵而伐齊，大破之。

translations.literal: The feudal lords saw Qi's exhaustion and ruin and the discord between ruler and ministers, raised troops to attack Qi, and greatly defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: The lords saw that Qi was exhausted and that its ruler and ministers were divided; they raised armies against Qi and crushed it.

sentences.zh: 士辱兵頓，皆咎其王，曰：『誰為此計者乎？』

translations.literal: Scholars humiliated troops weary, all blamed king, said: 'Who made this plan?'
translations.idiomatic: Scholars humiliated, troops weary, all blamed their king, saying: 'Who made this plan?'

sentences.zh: 王曰：『文子為之。』

translations.literal: The king said: 'Wen Zi did it.'
translations.idiomatic: The king said: 'Wen Zi did it.'

sentences.zh: 大臣作亂，文子出走。

translations.literal: The ministers made rebellion, and Wen Zi fled into exile.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers rebelled, and Wen Zi fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 攻齊所以大破者，以其伐楚而肥韓、魏也。

translations.literal: The reason the attack on Qi ended in great defeat was that attacking Chu had fattened Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The reason attacking Qi led to great defeat was because attacking Chu fattened Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 此所謂借賊兵而齎盜糧者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called borrowing a thief's troops and carrying a robber's grain.
translations.idiomatic: This is what they call borrowing a thief's troops and carrying a robber's grain.

sentences.zh: 王不如遠交而近攻，得寸則王之寸也，得尺亦王之尺也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should ally far and attack near—gain an inch and it becomes Your Majesty's inch, gain a foot and it becomes Your Majesty's foot.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should make distant alliances and attack nearby—every inch gained becomes Your Majesty's inch, every foot gained becomes Your Majesty's foot.

sentences.zh: 今釋此而遠攻，不亦繆乎！

translations.literal: Now abandoning this and attacking far away—is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Now abandoning this strategy and attacking distant targets—is this not utterly misguided!

sentences.zh: 且昔者中山之國地方五百里，趙獨吞之，功成名立而利附焉，天下莫之能害也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the past the state of Zhongshan had territory of five hundred li, Zhao alone swallowed it, merit accomplished and name established with benefits attached, the world none could harm it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the past the state of Zhongshan spanned five hundred li of territory. Zhao alone swallowed it whole, achieving merit and establishing reputation with benefits attached. None in the world could harm it.

sentences.zh: 今夫韓、魏，中國之處而天下之樞也，王其欲霸，必親中國以為天下樞，以威楚、趙。

translations.literal: Now as for Han and Wei, they are located in the central states and are the pivot of the world. If Your Majesty wishes to become hegemon, you must personally approach the central states as the world's pivot, to awe Chu and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Now consider Han and Wei—they occupy the central states and form the pivot of the world. If Your Majesty wishes to become hegemon, you must personally cultivate the central states as the world's pivot, using this to awe Chu and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 楚彊則附趙，趙彊則附楚，楚、趙皆附，齊必懼矣。

translations.literal: If Chu grows strong then attach to Zhao, if Zhao grows strong then attach to Chu. If Chu and Zhao both attach, Qi will certainly fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu grows strong, attach to Zhao; when Zhao grows strong, attach to Chu. Once both Chu and Zhao are attached, Qi will certainly fear.

sentences.zh: 齊懼，必卑辭重幣以事秦。

translations.literal: If Qi fears, it will certainly use humble words and heavy gifts to serve Qin.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi fears, it will certainly offer humble words and heavy tribute to serve Qin.

sentences.zh: 齊附而韓、魏因可虜也。」

translations.literal: If Qi attaches, then Han and Wei can consequently be captured.'
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi attaches, Han and Wei can consequently be taken captive.'

sentences.zh: 昭王曰：「吾欲親魏久矣，而魏多變之國也，寡人不能親。

translations.literal: King Zhao said, "I have long wished to be close to Wei, but Wei is a state of many changes, and I cannot be close to it.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao said, "I have long wished to draw Wei close, but Wei is a fickle state, and I cannot do it myself.

sentences.zh: 請問親魏柰何？」

translations.literal: Please ask personally Wei how?'
translations.idiomatic: May I ask how to visit Wei in person?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王卑詞重幣以事之；

translations.literal: He replied: 'With humble words and heavy gifts the king may serve him;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'When Your Majesty serves them with humble words and generous gifts,

sentences.zh: 不可，則割地而賂之；

translations.literal: If not possible, then cede land and bribe them;
translations.idiomatic: If that fails, cede land and bribe them;

sentences.zh: 不可，因舉兵而伐之。」

translations.literal: If not possible, then raise troops and attack them.'
translations.idiomatic: If that still fails, raise troops and attack them.'

sentences.zh: 王曰：「寡人敬聞命矣。」

translations.literal: The king said, "I respectfully hear your command."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "I respectfully accept your counsel."

sentences.zh: 乃拜范睢為客卿，謀兵事。

translations.literal: Thus, he appointed Fan Sui as guest minister to plan military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, he appointed Fan Sui as guest minister to plan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒聽范睢謀，使五大夫綰伐魏，拔懷。

translations.literal: In the end he listened to Fan Sui's plan, had Grand Master Wan of the fifth rank attack Wei and capture Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he followed Fan Sui's plan, sending Grand Master Wan of the fifth rank to attack Wei and capture Huai.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，拔邢丘。

translations.literal: Two years later, he captured Xingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, he captured Xingqiu.

sentences.zh: 客卿范睢復說昭王曰：「秦韓之地形，相錯如繡。

translations.literal: Guest minister Fan Sui again advised King Zhao: 'The land forms of Qin and Han interlock like embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Guest minister Fan Sui again advised King Zhao: 'The topography of Qin and Han interlocks like embroidery.

sentences.zh: 秦之有韓也，譬如木之有蠹也，人之有心腹之病也。

translations.literal: Qin having Han, like wood having borer, person having heart abdomen illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qin having Han is like wood having a borer, a person having a heart and abdomen illness.

sentences.zh: 天下無變則已，天下有變，其為秦患者孰大於韓乎？

translations.literal: World no change then stop, world has change, its for Qin patient who greater than Han?
translations.idiomatic: If the world remains unchanged, then that is one thing; but if the world changes, what greater affliction will Qin have than Han?

sentences.zh: 王不如收韓。」

translations.literal: King not equal take Han.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should take Han.'

sentences.zh: 昭王曰：「吾固欲收韓，韓不聽，為之柰何？」

translations.literal: Zhao Wang said: 'I indeed wish take Han, Han not listen, for it how?'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao said: 'I indeed wish to take Han, but Han won't listen—what can be done?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「韓安得無聽乎？

translations.literal: Replied: 'Han how not listen?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'How can Han not listen?

sentences.zh: 王下兵而攻滎陽，則鞏、成皋之道不通；

translations.literal: King send troops attack Xing Yang, then Gong, Cheng Gao way not through;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends troops to attack Xingyang, then the roads to Gong and Chenggao will be blocked;

sentences.zh: 北斷太行之道，則上黨之師不下。

translations.literal: North break Taihang way, then Shangdang troops not down.
translations.idiomatic: If northward you cut the Taihang roads, then Shangdang's troops cannot come down.

sentences.zh: 王一興兵而攻滎陽，則其國斷而為三。

translations.literal: King one raise troops attack Xing Yang, then its state cut as three.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty raises troops and attacks Xingyang once, then its state will be cut and divided into three.

sentences.zh: 夫韓見必亡，安得不聽乎？

translations.literal: Han see certainly perish, how not listen?
translations.idiomatic: Han seeing it will certainly perish, how can it not listen?

sentences.zh: 若韓聽，而霸事因可慮矣。」

translations.literal: If Han listen, hegemon matters then can consider.'
translations.idiomatic: If Han listens, then hegemon matters can consequently be considered.'

sentences.zh: 王曰：「善。」

translations.literal: King said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: The king said: 'Good.'

sentences.zh: 且欲發使於韓。

translations.literal: He also wished to send an envoy to Han.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to send an envoy to Han.

sentences.zh: 范睢日益親，復說用數年矣，因請閒說曰：「臣居山東時，聞齊之有田文，不聞其有王也；

translations.literal: Fan Sui grew daily more intimate, and after persuading the king for several years, he requested a private audience and said, "When I lived east of the mountains, I heard that Qi had Tian Wen; I did not hear that it had a king.
translations.idiomatic: As Fan Sui grew closer to the king and had advised him for several years, he requested a private audience and said, "When I lived east of the mountains, I heard that Qi had Tian Wen; I never heard that it had a king.

sentences.zh: 聞秦之有太后、穰侯、華陽、高陵、涇陽，不聞其有王也。

translations.literal: I heard that Qin had the Queen Mother, Lord Rang, Huayang, Gaoling, and Jingyang; I did not hear that it had a king.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, I heard that Qin had the Queen Mother, Lord Rang, Huayang, Gaoling, and Jingyang; I did not hear that Qin had a king.

sentences.zh: 夫擅國之謂王，能利害之謂王，制殺生之威之謂王。

translations.literal: One who monopolizes the state is called king; one who can bestow benefit and harm is called king; one who controls the authority over life and death is called king.
translations.idiomatic: The one who commands the state is the king; the one who can grant favor or inflict harm is the king; the one who holds power over life and death is the king.

sentences.zh: 今太后擅行不顧，穰侯出使不報，華陽、涇陽等擊斷無諱，高陵進退不請。

translations.literal: Now Queen Mother monopolize action not regard, Lord Rang out envoy not report, Huayang, Jingyang etc. attack cut no taboo, Gaoling advance retreat not request.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Queen Mother monopolizes actions without regard, Lord Rang goes on missions without reporting, Huayang, Jingyang and others attack and cut without taboo, Gaoling advances and retreats without requesting permission.

sentences.zh: 四貴備而國不危者，未之有也。

translations.literal: When the four nobles are complete and the state is not endangered, such a thing has never existed.
translations.idiomatic: There has never been a state with four such nobles in power that did not fall into danger.

sentences.zh: 為此四貴者下，乃所謂無王也。

translations.literal: To be below these four nobles is what is called having no king.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler stands beneath these four nobles, that is what it means for a state to have no king.

sentences.zh: 然則權安得不傾，令安得從王出乎？

translations.literal: If so, how can authority not tilt away, and how can commands issue from the king?
translations.idiomatic: If this continues, how can power fail to drift away, and how can commands still come from the king?

sentences.zh: 臣聞善治國者，乃內固其威而外重其權。

translations.literal: your servant has heard that those who are good at governing states solidify their might within and weight their authority without.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who are good at governing states solidify their might within and weight their authority without.

sentences.zh: 穰侯使者操王之重，決制於諸侯，剖符於天下，政適伐國，莫敢不聽。

translations.literal: Lord Rang envoys grasp king weight, decide at feudal lords, divide tallies world, politics suitable attack states, none dare not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Rang's envoys grasp the king's weight, decide matters among the feudal lords, divide tallies throughout the world, politics suitable for attacking states, none dare not listen.

sentences.zh: 戰勝攻取則利歸於陶，國獘御於諸侯；

translations.literal: Battle victory attack take then profit return Tao, state exhausted defend feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: Battle victories and conquests then profits return to Tao, state exhaustion defended against the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 戰敗則結怨於百姓，而禍歸於社稷。

translations.literal: Battle defeat then tie resentment hundred surnames, calamity return ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Battle defeats then tie resentment to the common people, and calamity returns to the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰『木實繁者披其枝，披其枝者傷其心；

translations.literal: Book of Odes said 'wood fruit dense peel branches, peel branches injure heart;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says 'wood with dense fruit peels its branches, peeling its branches injures its heart;

sentences.zh: 大其都者危其國，尊其臣者卑其主』。

translations.literal: Great cities danger state, honor ministers humble lord'.
translations.idiomatic: Greatening cities endangers the state, honoring ministers humbles the lord.

sentences.zh: 崔杼、淖齒管齊，射王股，擢王筋，縣之於廟梁，宿昔而死。

translations.literal: Cui Zhu, Nao Chi manage Qi, shoot king thigh, pluck king sinew, hang at temple beam, overnight died.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhu and Nao Chi managed Qi, shot the king's thigh, plucked the king's sinews, hung him from the temple beam, and he died overnight.

sentences.zh: 李兌管趙，囚主父於沙丘，百日而餓死。

translations.literal: Li Kui manage Zhao, imprisoned lord father Sha Qiu, hundred days starved died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui managed Zhao, imprisoned Lord Father at Shaqiu, and he starved to death after a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 今臣聞秦太后、穰侯用事，高陵、華陽、涇陽佐之，卒無秦王，此亦淖齒、李兌之類也。

translations.literal: Now minister heard Qin Queen Mother, Lord Rang employ affairs, Gaoling, Huayang, Jingyang assist, finally no Qin king, this also Nao Chi, Li Kui class.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have heard that Qin's Queen Mother and Lord Rang employ affairs, with Gaoling, Huayang, Jingyang assisting them, in the end there is no Qin king—this is also of the class of Nao Chi and Li Kui.

sentences.zh: 且夫三代所以亡國者，君專授政，縱酒馳騁弋獵，不聽政事。

translations.literal: Moreover, three dynasties what perished states, lord specialize grant politics, indulge wine race hunting, not listen politics.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reason the Three Dynasties perished their states was that the lords specialized in granting politics, indulged in wine, raced about hunting, did not listen to political affairs.

sentences.zh: 其所授者，妒賢嫉能，御下蔽上，以成其私，不為主計，而主不覺悟，故失其國。

translations.literal: Its granted, jealous worthy hate able, control under screen above, complete private, not for lord plan, lord not awaken, thus lose state.
translations.idiomatic: Those they granted were jealous of the worthy and hated the able, controlled below and screened above to complete their private interests, did not plan for the lord, and the lord did not awaken, thus they lost their state.

sentences.zh: 今自有秩以上至諸大吏，下及王左右，無非相國之人者。

translations.literal: Now from have rank above to various grand officials, down to king left right, none not chancellor people.
translations.idiomatic: Now from those with rank above to the various grand officials, down to the king's left and right, none are not the chancellor's people.

sentences.zh: 見王獨立於朝，臣竊為王恐，萬世之後，有秦國者非王子孫也。」

translations.literal: See king alone stand court, minister secretly for king fear, ten thousand generations after, have Qin none king sons grandsons.'
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the king alone stand in court, I secretly fear for the king—ten thousand generations later, those who have Qin will not be the king's sons and grandsons.'

sentences.zh: 昭王聞之大懼，曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Zhao Wang heard greatly fear, said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao heard this and was greatly frightened, saying: 'Good.'

sentences.zh: 於是廢太后，逐穰侯、高陵、華陽、涇陽君於關外。

translations.literal: Thereupon he deposed the Queen Mother and drove Lord Rang, Lord Gaoling, Lord Huayang, and Lord Jingyang beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He then stripped the Queen Mother of power and expelled Lord Rang, Lord Gaoling, Lord Huayang, and Lord Jingyang beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 秦王乃拜范睢為相。

translations.literal: The King of Qin then appointed Fan Sui as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin then made Fan Sui his chancellor.

sentences.zh: 收穰侯之印，使歸陶，因使縣官給車牛以徙，千乘有餘。

translations.literal: He took back Lord Rang's seal, made him return to Tao, and had the county officials supply carts and oxen for the move, more than a thousand carts in all.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Lord Rang's seal, sent him back to Tao, and ordered the county officials to provide carts and oxen for his removal, more than a thousand carts altogether.

sentences.zh: 到關，關閱其寶器，寶器珍怪多於王室。

translations.literal: Arrived pass, pass inspected treasures, treasures precious strange many over royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived at the pass, the pass officials inspected his treasures—his treasures were precious and strange, many more than the royal house.

sentences.zh: 秦封范睢以應，號為應侯。

translations.literal: Qin sealed Fan Sui with Ying, number Ying Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin sealed Fan Sui with Ying, calling him Ying Hou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，秦昭王四十一年也。

translations.literal: At this time it was the forty-first year of King Zhao of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, it was the forty-first year of Qin King Zhao.

sentences.zh: 范睢既相秦，秦號曰張祿，而魏不知，以為范睢已死久矣。

translations.literal: Fan Sui had already become chancellor of Qin; Qin called him Zhang Lu, but Wei did not know this and thought Fan Sui had long been dead.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui had already become chancellor of Qin, and Qin called him Zhang Lu, but Wei did not know, considering that Fan Sui had died long ago.

sentences.zh: 魏聞秦且東伐韓、魏，魏使須賈於秦。

translations.literal: Wei heard that Qin was about to attack Han and Wei eastward, so Wei sent Xu Jia to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei heard that Qin was preparing to campaign east against Han and Wei, it sent Xu Jia to Qin.

sentences.zh: 范睢聞之，為微行，敝衣閒步之邸，見須賈。

translations.literal: Fan Sui heard of this and traveled in secret, dressed in ragged clothes, and leisurely strolled into the hostel to see Xu Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui heard this and traveled in secret, dressed in ragged clothes, and leisurely strolled into the hostel to see Xu Jia.

sentences.zh: 須賈見之而驚曰：「范叔固無恙乎！」

translations.literal: Xu Jia saw him and was startled, saying, "Uncle Fan, are you truly well!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia saw him and started in surprise: "Uncle Fan, you are alive and well!"

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Yes.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'It is so.'

sentences.zh: 須賈笑曰：「范叔有說於秦邪？」

translations.literal: Xu Jia laughed: 'Fan Shu have persuasion at Qin?'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia laughed and said: 'Uncle Fan, do you have persuasion in Qin?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「不也。

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'Not so.

sentences.zh: 睢前日得過於魏相，故亡逃至此，安敢說乎！」

translations.literal: I earlier incurred offense with the Wei chancellor and therefore fled here; how would I dare offer persuasion!"
translations.idiomatic: I offended the Wei chancellor earlier and fled here because of it. How would I dare come as a persuader!"

sentences.zh: 須賈曰：「今叔何事？」

translations.literal: Xu Jia said: 'Now uncle what matter?'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia said: 'Now Uncle, what are you doing?'

sentences.zh: 范睢曰「臣為人庸賃。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Your servant is hired labor for others.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'I am a hired laborer for others.'

sentences.zh: 須賈意哀之，留與坐飲食，曰：「范叔一寒如此哉！」

translations.literal: Xu Jia pitied, left with sit eat drink, said: 'Fan Shu one cold like this!'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia pitied him, had him stay and sit to eat and drink, saying: 'Uncle Fan, are you so cold as this!'

sentences.zh: 乃取其一綈袍以賜之。

translations.literal: Then he took one silk robe and granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then took one of his silk robes and granted it to him.

sentences.zh: 須賈因問曰：「秦相張君，公知之乎？

translations.literal: Xu Jia then asked: 'The Qin chancellor Zhang Jun—do you know him?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia then asked: 'Qin Chancellor Zhang Jun, do you know him?

sentences.zh: 吾聞幸於王，天下之事皆決於相君。

translations.literal: I have heard he is favored by the king; all affairs under heaven are decided by Chancellor Jun.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard he is favored by the king, and all world matters are decided by Chancellor Jun.

sentences.zh: 今吾事之去留在張君。

translations.literal: Now whether my mission succeeds or fails rests with Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Now whether my matter succeeds or fails depends on Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 孺子豈有客習於相君者哉？」

translations.literal: How could a youth like me have a guest acquainted with the Chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: How could someone as lowly as I have a guest who knows the Chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「主人翁習知之。

translations.literal: Fan Sui said, "The master of the house knows him well.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui replied, "My host knows him well.

sentences.zh: 唯睢亦得謁，睢請為見君於張君。」

translations.literal: Only if Sui also obtains an audience will Sui request to present you to Zhang Jun.'
translations.idiomatic: Only if Sui also gets an audience, Sui will request to see Jun at Zhang Jun.'

sentences.zh: 須賈曰：「吾馬病，車軸折，非大車駟馬，吾固不出。」

translations.literal: Xu Jia said: 'My horse ill, carriage axle broke, not great carriage four horses, I certainly not out.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia said: 'My horse is ill, the carriage axle is broken, without a great carriage and four horses, I certainly won't go out.'

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「願為君借大車駟馬於主人翁。」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'Wish for jun borrow great carriage four horses at host master.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'I wish to borrow a great carriage and four horses for you from the host master.'

sentences.zh: 范睢歸取大車駟馬，為須賈御之，入秦相府。

translations.literal: Fan Sui returned took great carriage four horses, for Xu Jia drove, entered Qin chancellor residence.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui returned and took a great carriage and four horses, drove it for Xu Jia, and entered the Qin chancellor's residence.

sentences.zh: 府中望見，有識者皆避匿。

translations.literal: In residence saw, those who recognized all hid away.
translations.idiomatic: In the residence, those who saw him and recognized him all hid themselves.

sentences.zh: 須賈怪之。

translations.literal: Xu Jia found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia was surprised by this.

sentences.zh: 至相舍門，謂須賈曰：「待我，我為君先入通於相君。」

translations.literal: Arrived chancellor residence gate, told Xu Jia: 'Wait me, I for jun first enter announce at chancellor jun.'
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at the chancellor's residence gate, he told Xu Jia: 'Wait for me, I will enter first to announce you to the chancellor.'

sentences.zh: 須賈待門下，持車良久，問門下曰：「范叔不出，何也？」

translations.literal: Xu Jia waited at gate, held carriage long time, asked gate keeper: 'Fan Shu not out, why?'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia waited at the gate, held the carriage for a long time, asked the gatekeeper: 'Why hasn't Uncle Fan come out?'

sentences.zh: 門下曰：「無范叔。」

translations.literal: Gate keeper said: 'No Fan Shu.'
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper said: 'There is no Uncle Fan.'

sentences.zh: 須賈曰：「鄉者與我載而入者。」

translations.literal: Xu Jia said: 'Just now with me loaded entered.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia said: 'The one who just entered with me in the carriage.'

sentences.zh: 門下曰：「乃吾相張君也。」

translations.literal: Gate keeper said: 'That is our chancellor Zhang jun.'
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper said: 'That is our Chancellor Zhang Jun.'

sentences.zh: 須賈大驚，自知見賣，乃肉袒厀行，因門下人謝罪。

translations.literal: Xu Jia was greatly startled; knowing he had been tricked, he bared his flesh and went on his knees, apologizing for his crime through the gatekeeper.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia was greatly startled, realized he had been tricked, then bared his flesh and crawled on his knees, apologizing for his crime through the gatekeeper.

sentences.zh: 於是范睢盛帷帳，待者甚眾，見之。

translations.literal: Then Fan Sui set up abundant curtains and tents, with attendants very numerous, and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, Fan Sui set up abundant curtains and tents, with attendants very numerous, and saw him.

sentences.zh: 須賈頓首言死罪，曰：「賈不意君能自致於青雲之上，賈不敢復讀天下之書，不敢復與天下之事。

translations.literal: Xu Jia knocked his head and spoke of his death crime, saying: 'Jia did not expect that you could raise yourself to the azure clouds; Jia dares not again read the books of the world or again engage in the affairs of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia kowtowed and confessed his death crime, saying: 'Jia did not expect Jun could achieve the azure clouds above, Jia dares not again read the world's books, dares not again participate in the world's matters.

sentences.zh: 賈有湯鑊之罪，請自屏於胡貉之地，唯君死生之！」

translations.literal: Jia have boiling cauldron crime, please self screen at Hu Mo land, only jun life death!'
translations.idiomatic: Jia has the crime of the boiling cauldron, please screen myself at the land of the Hu and Mo, only Jun's life and death!'

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「汝罪有幾？」

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'You crime have how many?'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'How many crimes do you have?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「擢賈之發以續賈之罪，尚未足。」

translations.literal: Said: 'Pluck Jia hair continue Jia crime, not yet sufficient.'
translations.idiomatic: Said: 'Pluck Jia's hair to continue Jia's crimes, not yet sufficient.'

sentences.zh: 范睢曰：「汝罪有三耳。

translations.literal: Fan Sui said: 'You crime have three only.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui said: 'You have three crimes only.

sentences.zh: 昔者楚昭王時而申包胥為楚卻吳軍，楚王封之以荊五千戶，包胥辭不受，為丘墓之寄於荊也。

translations.literal: In past Chu Zhao Wang time Shen Bao Xu for Chu repelled Wu army, Chu king sealed him with Jing five thousand households, Shen Bao Xu declined not accept, because ancestral mounds entrusted in Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the past when King Zhao of Chu was in power, Shen Baoxu for Chu repelled the Wu army, the Chu king sealed him with five thousand households in Jing, but Shen Baoxu declined to accept, because his ancestral mounds were entrusted in Jing.

sentences.zh: 今睢之先人丘墓亦在魏，公前以睢為有外心於齊而惡睢於魏齊，公之罪一也。

translations.literal: Now Sui ancestors mounds tombs also at Wei, you before considered Sui have disloyalty toward Qi slandered Sui to Wei Qi, you crime one.
translations.idiomatic: Now Sui's ancestors' mounds and tombs are also in Wei, before you considered Sui to have disloyalty toward Qi and slandered Sui to Wei Qi—this is your crime one.

sentences.zh: 當魏齊辱我於廁中，公不止，罪二也。

translations.literal: When Wei Qi humiliated me at latrine middle, you not stop, crime two.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Qi humiliated me in the latrine, you did not stop him—this is crime two.

sentences.zh: 更醉而溺我，公其何忍乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, drunk urinated me, you how bear?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, drunk, he urinated on me—how could you bear this?

sentences.zh: 罪三矣。

translations.literal: Crime three.
translations.idiomatic: This is crime three.

sentences.zh: 然公之所以得無死者，以綈袍戀戀，有故人之意，故釋公。」

translations.literal: However, you what get no die, with silk robe lingering, have old friend intent, thus released you.'
translations.idiomatic: However, the reason you got to not die is because of the lingering silk robe, having old friend's intent, thus I released you.'

sentences.zh: 乃謝罷。

translations.literal: Thus, thanked dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, he thanked and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 入言之昭王，罷歸須賈。

translations.literal: Entered spoke Zhao Wang, dismissed returned Xu Jia.
translations.idiomatic: He entered and spoke to King Zhao, dismissed and returned Xu Jia.

sentences.zh: 須賈辭於范睢，范睢大供具，盡請諸侯使，與坐堂上，食飲甚設。

translations.literal: Xu Jia took leave at Fan Sui, Fan Sui greatly provided utensils, completely invited feudal lords envoys, with sat hall above, food drink abundantly set.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jia took leave of Fan Sui, Fan Sui prepared a lavish array of vessels, invited all the feudal lords' envoys, seated them in the hall above, and set out abundant food and drink.

sentences.zh: 而坐須賈於堂下，置莝豆其前，令兩黥徒夾而馬食之。

translations.literal: Yet sat Xu Jia at hall below, placed bean stalks before, commanded two tattooed convicts flank horse feed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet seated Xu Jia in the hall below, placed bean stalks before him, commanded two tattooed convicts to flank and horse-feed him.

sentences.zh: 數曰：「為我告魏王，急持魏齊頭來！

translations.literal: Scolded said: 'For me tell Wei king, urgent hold Wei Qi head come!
translations.idiomatic: He scolded saying: 'For me tell the Wei king, urgently bring Wei Qi's head!

sentences.zh: 不然者，我且屠大梁。」

translations.literal: Not then, I moreover butcher Daliang.'
translations.idiomatic: If not, I will moreover butcher Daliang.'

sentences.zh: 須賈歸，以告魏齊。

translations.literal: Xu Jia returned, with told Wei Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia returned and told Wei Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏齊恐，亡走趙。

translations.literal: Wei Qi became afraid and fled to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qi was frightened and fled to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 匿平原君所。

translations.literal: He hid at Lord Pingyuan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: He went into hiding with Lord Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 范睢既相，王稽謂范睢曰：「事有不可知者三，有不柰何者亦三。

translations.literal: After Fan Sui became chancellor, Wang Ji said to him, "There are three things in affairs that cannot be known, and three things for which there is no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Sui became chancellor, Wang Ji told him, "There are three things no one can foresee, and three things no one can remedy.

sentences.zh: 宮車一日晏駕，是事之不可知者一也。

translations.literal: If the palace carriage one day departs late, this is the first thing that cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If the royal carriage should one day be late in setting out, that is the first unforeseen thing.

sentences.zh: 君卒然捐館舍，是事之不可知者二也。

translations.literal: If Your Lordship suddenly abandons your lodging, this is the second thing that cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Lordship should suddenly leave this world, that is the second unforeseen thing.

sentences.zh: 使臣卒然填溝壑，是事之不可知者三也。

translations.literal: If I should suddenly fill the ditches and ravines, this is the third thing that cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If I should suddenly end up dead in a ditch, that is the third unforeseen thing.

sentences.zh: 宮車一日晏駕，君雖恨於臣，無可柰何。

translations.literal: Palace carriage one day late start, lord though hate minister, no can how.
translations.idiomatic: If one day the royal carriage sets out late, even if Your Lordship hates me, there will be nothing you can do.

sentences.zh: 君卒然捐館舍，君雖恨於臣，亦無可柰何。

translations.literal: Lord suddenly abandon dwelling, lord though hate minister, also no can how.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Lordship suddenly abandons your dwelling, even if you hate me, there will likewise be nothing you can do.

sentences.zh: 使臣卒然填溝壑，君雖恨於臣，亦無可柰何。」

translations.literal: Make minister suddenly fill ditch moat, lord though hate minister, also no can how.'
translations.idiomatic: If I should suddenly fill the ditches and ravines, even if Your Lordship hates me, there will likewise be nothing you can do.'

sentences.zh: 范睢不懌，乃入言於王曰：「非王稽之忠，莫能內臣於函谷關；

translations.literal: Fan Sui was displeased and went in to speak to the king, saying, "Without Wang Ji's loyalty, no one could have brought me inside Hangu Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui was displeased. He went in to the king and said, "Had Wang Ji not been loyal, no one could have brought me through Hangu Pass;

sentences.zh: 非大王之賢聖，莫能貴臣。

translations.literal: without Your Majesty's wisdom and sagacity, no one could have honored me.
translations.idiomatic: and had Your Majesty not been wise and discerning, no one could have raised me to honor.

sentences.zh: 今臣官至於相，爵在列侯，王稽之官尚止於謁者，非其內臣之意也。」

translations.literal: Now my office has reached the chancellorship and my rank is among the listed marquises, but Wang Ji's office still stops at receptionist; this is not my intention toward the man who brought me in."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have become chancellor and rank among the marquises, while Wang Ji remains merely a receptionist. That is not how I meant to treat the man who brought me in."

sentences.zh: 昭王召王稽，拜為河東守，三歲不上計。

translations.literal: King Zhao summoned Wang Ji and appointed him governor of Hedong, and for three years he did not submit accounts.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao summoned Wang Ji and made him governor of Hedong, where he went three years without submitting accounts.

sentences.zh: 又任鄭安平，昭王以為將軍。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zheng Anping, and King Zhao made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui also recommended Zheng Anping, whom King Zhao made a general.

sentences.zh: 范睢於是散家財物，盡以報所嘗困戹者。

translations.literal: Fan Sui then scattered family wealth goods, all with repay once distressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Sui then distributed his family wealth, using it all to repay those who had once helped him in distress.

sentences.zh: 一飯之德必償，睚眥之怨必報。

translations.literal: One meal virtue certainly repay, glare enmity certainly report.
translations.idiomatic: He repaid even the kindness of a single meal, and avenged even the resentment born of a glare.

sentences.zh: 范睢相秦二年，秦昭王之四十二年，東伐韓少曲、高平，拔之。

translations.literal: Fan Sui chancellor Qin two years, Qin Zhao Wang forty two year, east attacked Han Shao Qu, Gao Ping, captured.
translations.idiomatic: In Fan Sui's second year as chancellor of Qin, the forty-second year of King Zhao of Qin, Qin attacked Han's Shaoqu and Gaoping in the east and captured them.

sentences.zh: 秦昭王聞魏齊在平原君所，欲為范睢必報其仇，乃詳為好書遺平原君曰；

translations.literal: King Zhao of Qin heard that Wei Qi was at Lord Pingyuan's residence and, wishing to avenge Fan Sui's grievance, feigned a friendly letter and sent it to Lord Pingyuan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhao of Qin heard that Wei Qi was staying with Lord Pingyuan, he wanted to avenge Fan Sui. He therefore sent Lord Pingyuan a letter pretending friendship:

sentences.zh: 「寡人聞君之高義，願與君為布衣之友，君幸過寡人，寡人願與君為十日之飲。」

translations.literal: "I have heard of Your Lordship's lofty righteousness and wish to be your plain-clothed friend. If Your Lordship would favor me with a visit, I would like to drink with you for ten days."
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard of Your Lordship's noble conduct and would like to be your friend as a common man. If you honor me with a visit, I would like to drink with you for ten days."

sentences.zh: 平原君畏秦，且以為然，而入秦見昭王。

translations.literal: Lord Pingyuan feared Qin and also thought this was sincere, so he entered Qin to see King Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pingyuan feared Qin and took the letter at face value, so he went to Qin to see King Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭王與平原君飲數日，昭王謂平原君曰：「昔周文王得呂尚以為太公，齊桓公得管夷吾以為仲父，今范君亦寡人之叔父也。

translations.literal: King Zhao drank with Lord Pingyuan for several days, then said to him, "Formerly King Wen of Zhou obtained Lü Shang and made him Grand Duke; Duke Huan of Qi obtained Guan Yiwu and made him Uncle Zhong. Now Lord Fan is likewise my uncle.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao drank with Lord Pingyuan for several days, then said, "In the past, King Wen of Zhou found Lü Shang and made him his Grand Duke; Duke Huan of Qi found Guan Yiwu and made him Uncle Zhong. Lord Fan is likewise an uncle to me.

sentences.zh: 范君之仇在君之家，願使人歸取其頭來；

translations.literal: Lord Fan's enemy is in Your Lordship's house; I wish to send men back to fetch his head.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Fan's enemy is in your house. I want to send men back with you to bring me his head.

sentences.zh: 不然，吾不出君於關。」

translations.literal: If not, I will not send Your Lordship out through the pass."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I will not let you leave the pass."

sentences.zh: 平原君曰：「貴而為交者，為賤也；

translations.literal: Lord Pingyuan said, "When the noble make friends, it is for the sake of the humble;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pingyuan replied, "When men of rank make friends, they do so for men without rank;

sentences.zh: 富而為交者，為貧也。

translations.literal: when the rich make friends, it is for the sake of the poor.
translations.idiomatic: when the wealthy make friends, they do so for the poor.

sentences.zh: 夫魏齊者，勝之友也，在，固不出也，今又不在臣所。」

translations.literal: Wei Qi is my friend; if he were present, I certainly would not send him out, and now he is not at my residence."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qi is my friend. If he were with me, I would certainly not hand him over; as it happens, he is not in my residence."

sentences.zh: 昭王乃遺趙王書曰：「王之弟在秦，范君之仇魏齊在平原君之家。

translations.literal: King Zhao then sent a letter to the King of Zhao, saying: 'Your younger brother is in Qin; Lord Fan's enemy Wei Qi is in Lord Pingyuan's house.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao then sent a letter to the King of Zhao, saying: 'Your Majesty's younger brother is in Qin; Lord Fan's enemy Wei Qi is in Lord Pingyuan's house.

sentences.zh: 王使人疾持其頭來；

translations.literal: The king should send people to hurry and bring his head here;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, send people to hurry and bring his head here;

sentences.zh: 不然，吾舉兵而伐趙，又不出王之弟於關。」

translations.literal: Not, I raise troops attack Zhao, again not out king younger brother at pass.'
translations.idiomatic: If not, I will raise troops and attack Zhao, and again not let your younger brother leave the pass.'

sentences.zh: 趙孝成王乃發卒圍平原君家，急，魏齊夜亡出，見趙相虞卿。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiao Cheng Wang then sent troops surrounded Ping Yuan Jun house, urgent, Wei Qi night fled out, saw Zhao chancellor Yu Qing.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiaocheng of Zhao then sent troops to surround Lord Pingyuan's house. It became urgent, Wei Qi fled out at night and saw Zhao's chancellor Yu Qing.

sentences.zh: 虞卿度趙王終不可說，乃解其相印，與魏齊亡，閒行，念諸侯莫可以急抵者，乃復走大梁，欲因信陵君以走楚。

translations.literal: Yu Qing measured Zhao Wang finally not can persuade, then untied chancellor seal, with Wei Qi fled, hidden walk, thought various lords none can urgent reach, then again ran Daliang, wished because Xinling Jun flee Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing measured that the King of Zhao could ultimately not be persuaded, thus he untied his chancellor seal and fled with Wei Qi, traveling in secret. He thought that none of the feudal lords could be urgently reached, thus he again ran to Daliang, wishing to use Lord Xinling to flee to Chu.

sentences.zh: 信陵君聞之，畏秦，猶豫未肯見，曰：「虞卿何如人也？」

translations.literal: Xinling Jun heard, feared Qin, hesitated not willing see, said: 'Yu Qing what like person?'
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xinling heard this, feared Qin, hesitated and was not willing to see them, saying: 'What kind of person is Yu Qing?'
